The repository's process rules about commits, pull requests, release notes and lesson or changelog files belong to the orchestrator, not this task: judge the change against the task and its criteria, and do not fail it for those.

Verdict rule: FAIL only for an unmet acceptance criterion or a P0/P1 finding. P2/P3 findings are reported with a PASS verdict. Start each finding with its severity (P0-P3).
Report only correctness bugs and requirement gaps (an acceptance criterion the diff does not meet). Set `kind` on each finding: `correctness` or `requirement`; style, naming and nits are `style` or `nit` and never block. Where you can, give a `scenario`: the shell command or test (`run`) that fails because of the finding and the failure it shows (`fails`). A finding that comes back after it was fixed is kept only with a new failing scenario. Set `causedByDiff` on each finding: true when the diff introduces the problem or breaks something that depended on the code it changed (a caller the diff did not touch counts), false when the problem was already there and the diff does not affect it.

## Report format

Reply with:

```sushi-review
{"verdict":"PASS|FAIL","findings":[{"finding":"P2: path:line - issue","id":"<registered id or null>","causedByDiff":true,"kind":"correctness|requirement|style|nit","scenario":{"run":"<shell command or test>","fails":"<the failure it shows>"}}],"criteria":[{"criterion":0,"met":true,"evidence":"..."}]}
```

Rule on every acceptance criterion, using its `check:` where it has one and the verify results as evidence. Fill in the `criteria` array of the one JSON object in your reply, `{"criterion":<number>,"met":true|false|null,"evidence":"..."}` per criterion, where `criterion` is the number the criterion has in the list above (a number, not its text), with `null` for a criterion you cannot check read-only. The verdict is PASS only if no criterion is `false`; a claim in the task that the code contradicts is a finding.
